title: When the Monsoon Falls
premise: Wren Thackeray, estranged from their famous archaeologist father and living as a freelance surveyor across the monsoon belt, is hired to trace a vanished government team in the flooded hills of the Konkan coast. What Wren finds is the team alive, guarding a temple complex whose artifacts could invalidate the mining concession that a powerful minister's family has held for generations. As the permits' expiration nears, Wren must smuggle the team and the evidence out through rising floodwaters while dodging hired enforcers, and must decide whether exposing the truth will cost the local villagers the only protection the site's secrecy ever gave them. In the end, Wren burns the official survey but leaves the evidence with the villagers, choosing justice outside the law and, finally, a letter home.
about_author: Odile Thackeray is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping river basins across South Asia before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who measure their lives in miles rather than years.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hired quietly by a desperate ministry clerk, Wren treks into the monsoon-soaked hills to find the vanished survey team, finding only abandoned gear, a torn permit, and no tracks. The beat: reluctant competence masking grief, as the landscape stirs memories of the father who taught them to read terrain and then chose ambition over family.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, shifting to team leader Iyer's journal entries. Wren locates the team hiding in a submerged temple cave, guarding artifacts proving the concession land was never crown property. Enforcers arrive at the village below. The beat: the vertigo of inherited power, as Wren realizes their father's name is on the original fraudulent grant.

chapters.title: Permits and Floodlines
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren and Iyer POV. With the permits expiring at dawn, the group moves the evidence through flood tunnels while enforcers close in; a villager girl, Meera, guides them through passages only locals know. Iyer is wounded covering the retreat. The beat: trust forged under pressure, and Wren's growing conviction that the law itself is the trap.

chapters.title: Everything the Monsoon Returns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the district office, Wren faces the minister's son with a choice: sell the artifacts' location for safety, or burn the survey and let the flood reclaim the secret. Wren burns it, delivers the originals to the village council, and walks out into the rain. The beat: release, as Wren finally writes to their father, measuring life in miles no longer.
